newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian opposition demands delay in election.
newsitem.headline: Croatian opposition demands delay in election.

text.p: Croatia's opposition Social Liberal party called on Tuesday for Sunday's presidential election to be postponed by two weeks after its candidate Vlado Gotovac was attacked at a campaign rally.

"The reason for this is the attempt on the life of Vlado Gotovac in Pula...when he sustained such injuries that he was thrown out of the presidential race," party secretary Karl Gorinsek told a news conference.

Gotovac suffered concussion and neck injuries after being hit on the head with a belt buckle. He was treated in hospital and doctors said on Monday he had to refrain from any activity and stay in bed.

The party asked for both other candidates, President Franjo Tudjman and Zdravko Tomac of the Social Democrats, to stop campaigning until Gotovac is better. They said Gotovac should be allowed to add on days he has lost to lengthen his campaign.

"There is no legal or constitutional barrier for this to be done. The electoral committee of the Republic of Croatia should have looked into the state of the campaign and called for this themselves," said party official Slavko Bokvic.

The party released the findings of a doctor's examination which found that Gotovac was suffering from a recurrence of neck injuries which he sustained during his time in prison after he was jailed for supporting Croatia's pro-independence movement in the 1970s.
The Liberal party said if their demand was not met Gotovac would still stand as a candidate in Sunday's vote and rumours of him withdrawing were absolutely false, Gorinsek said.

The man who attacked Gotovac was a captain in the Croatian army and was in uniform at the time. The ministry of defence named him as Tomislav Brzovic, said he was drunk at the time of the attack and immediately suspended him from duty and detained him.
The Liberal party and independent weekly news magazine Feral Tribune both alleged Brzovic was a member of Tudjman's elite security guard though this has not been confirmed by the ministry of defence.
Gorinsek said Brzovic had been released from military jail and taken to a civilian prison in Pula. This was an indication, he said, that Brzovic must have been dishonourably discharged from the army.
Both opposition candidates are fighting a losing battle to try and oust Tudjman, who is widely expected to win the election in the first round.
They face fawning state-run media which run at length many of the president's official engagements, ensuring he benefits from more coverage than his opponents do.
One opposition party supporting Gotovac as its candidate accused Tudjman, his party and state television of satanising all opposition leaders and fuelling the idea they were enemies of the state.

"Standing in these elections is a gesture aimed to show against all the odds that there is another Croatia which resists the present ruling style...and that there are people who are displeased with it," Gotovac told Reuters recently.
